references.title: Counter-Strike 2
observedFacts: Valve positions Counter-Strike as a long-running competitive first-person team game and CS2 as the Source 2 successor.
The product is tagged and presented around tactical, competitive, team-based PvP rather than persistent character progression.
causalHypotheses: Short round resets plus lethal commitment make positional and information mistakes legible and costly.
A comparatively stable ruleset lets mastery accumulate in aiming, movement, map knowledge, timing and team coordination.
transferHypotheses: A tiny round-based objective can test whether partial information plus irreversible death creates meaningful positional commitment.
references.smallestFalsifiableBaseline: One graybox objective map, two teams, one weapon family, lethal elimination, partial information and immediate round reset; add economy only if the tested claim needs inter-round resource commitment.
references.baselineFalsifier: If removing partial information or lethal round commitment does not materially change player positioning, information seeking or tension, the proposed transfer is weak.

references.title: Dota 2
observedFacts: Valve describes a battlefield with more than one hundred heroes, diverse abilities and items, and heroes that can fill multiple roles.
The product is continuously updated and explicitly emphasizes strategic variety and replayability rather than a fixed campaign.
causalHypotheses: Long-horizon power curves turn early local choices into later teamfight and objective consequences.
Hero-role and item combinatorics create adaptation pressure both before and during a match.
Shared objectives make individual optimization insufficient without team coordination.
expressionDependencies: combat readability across many simultaneous effects
transferHypotheses: A one-lane micro-MOBA can test whether role asymmetry plus shared objective pressure creates meaningful coordination and timing decisions.
references.smallestFalsifiableBaseline: One lane, two roles per side, minion pressure, one tower/objective, simple experience/item timing and a bounded teamfight end condition.
references.baselineFalsifier: If players can independently maximize local damage without communicating or trading resources/timing for the shared objective, the role-interdependence hypothesis is weak.

references.title: Fortnite
observedFacts: Epic currently exposes Battle Royale and Zero Build as separate high-stakes variants, with Ranked progression influenced by placement, eliminations, damage and storm-circle survival.
Fortnite is also a creator ecosystem with UEFN/Creative publishing, playtests, analytics and monetization; it is not one mechanic or one mode.
causalHypotheses: One-life match structure plus shrinking safe space creates repeated movement-versus-engagement tradeoffs.
Loot uncertainty and spatial information make adaptation central to each run.
The wider ecosystem may sustain longevity through social presence, rapid content change and creator variety beyond Battle Royale itself.
transferHypotheses: A tiny shrinking-arena survival experiment can isolate whether uncertainty plus forced convergence produces meaningful risk timing without reproducing Fortnite's ecosystem.
references.smallestFalsifiableBaseline: Eight-entity arena, sparse loot choices, one life, shrinking safe area, optional combat and clear placement outcome; building excluded from first baseline and tested separately.
references.baselineFalsifier: If the shrinking boundary and one-life condition do not alter route, engagement or resource decisions compared with a static respawn arena, the BR transfer hypothesis is weak.

references.title: Minecraft
observedFacts: Mojang explicitly states that Minecraft has no single required goal and supports player-chosen play.
Blocks can be broken, crafted and placed to reshape the world; Survival adds resource collection, danger, health/hunger and tool constraints, while Creative removes those constraints.
causalHypotheses: A low-level reversible world-manipulation vocabulary lets players convert personal intentions into persistent spatial outcomes.
Survival constraints can generate reasons to explore and build without replacing self-authored goals.
The same block grammar supports construction, traversal, collection, survival and social play, increasing recombination value.
transferHypotheses: Self-authored intention can be tested with a very small persistent construction grammar rather than a large procedural world.
references.smallestFalsifiableBaseline: A compact block field with break, obtain and place actions plus one environmental constraint; no authored objective beyond a neutral invitation to change the space.
references.baselineFalsifier: If players do not form their own spatial intention or if persistent transformation does not affect subsequent behavior, the authorship hypothesis is weak.

references.title: Grand Theft Auto V
observedFacts: Rockstar presents Los Santos/Blaine County as the shared setting for a story campaign and the evolving GTA Online product.
GTA Online supports cooperative heists, races, adversary modes, businesses, vehicles and social spaces for up to 30 players.
causalHypotheses: A dense shared world that supports driving, combat, traversal and social interaction makes changing activity feel continuous rather than menu-isolated.
Escalating world response can make unscripted actions generate their own short causal stories.
Vehicle access radically changes traversal affordances and the perceived possibility space.
transferHypotheses: Systemic freedom can be tested in one small district if actions cross subsystem boundaries and the world responds consistently.
references.smallestFalsifiableBaseline: One city block, walking/driving, vehicle acquisition, simple civilian/world response, escalating law pressure and at least two escape routes.
references.baselineFalsifier: If players treat verbs as isolated minigames and do not improvise plans from cross-system interactions, the systemic-freedom hypothesis is weak.

references.title: ELDEN RING
observedFacts: Bandai Namco describes a seamless large world plus complex dungeons, with traversal on foot/horseback and many combat approaches.
Official guidance explicitly says players may avoid powerful enemies and return later, and that there is not one required path or build.
Combat guidance emphasizes reading enemy intent, timing dodge/parry/guard and selecting among weapons, magic, stealth, summons and allies.
causalHypotheses: High-cost enemy commitment windows make observation and timing learnable forms of mastery.
Open routing converts difficulty from a binary wall into a strategic choice to persist, explore or return later.
Build variety and optional assistance broaden viable solutions without removing encounter identity.
transferHypotheses: The combat mastery claim can be isolated in one duel; the open-routing claim requires a separate multi-route environment experiment.
references.smallestFalsifiableBaseline: One graybox duel with readable telegraph, committed attack, evade/block, punish window, limited resource, death and fast retry; separate second condition allows bypass/return-later routing.
references.baselineFalsifier: If repeated attempts do not change anticipation/timing or if removing commitment windows leaves the same behavior, the mastery hypothesis is weak.

references.title: Baldur's Gate 3
observedFacts: Larian presents BG3 as a party RPG where choices shape relationships and outcomes, with multiple Origin perspectives and four-player co-op.
Its combat uses D&D-derived turn-based rules, initiative, advantage/disadvantage and environmental interaction.
Larian documented changing combat ordering during Early Access based on feedback/testing and supports forced turn-based exploration for stealth/puzzle planning.
causalHypotheses: Agency becomes credible when multiple mechanically different approaches are acknowledged by later world/narrative state.
Systemic environment interactions make problem solving broader than dialogue-option branching.
Party composition and companion reactions give decisions social as well as tactical consequence.
transferHypotheses: A tiny authored situation can test whether multiple valid approaches plus later acknowledgement create perceived agency without reproducing a full CRPG.
references.smallestFalsifiableBaseline: One situation with three mechanically distinct approaches, persistent consequence state, one companion/observer reaction and a later scene that acknowledges the chosen path.
references.baselineFalsifier: If players perceive the approaches as cosmetic equivalents, or later acknowledgement does not change interpretation of the choice, the reactivity hypothesis is weak.

references.title: Factorio
observedFacts: Wube defines the core around mining resources, logistics, production, infrastructure, research, automation, energy and defense.
The official description explicitly moves from manual collection/crafting toward increasingly automated industrial systems.
causalHypotheses: Automation turns prior manual effort into persistent capability, creating a strong visible sense of leverage.
Bottlenecks make system state diagnostically legible: throughput problems suggest concrete redesign actions.
Expansion creates self-generated complexity because each solution increases resource and coordination demands elsewhere.
transferHypotheses: Automation value can be tested with a four-stage production chain and visible throughput before any large tech tree exists.
references.smallestFalsifiableBaseline: Source -> transport -> processor -> sink, with limited power and one throughput target; allow redesign while preserving production history.
references.baselineFalsifier: If automation does not change player planning from repeated execution toward diagnosis/architecture, or bottlenecks remain opaque, the leverage hypothesis is weak.

references.title: Mario Kart 8 Deluxe
observedFacts: Nintendo exposes drift, rocket start, mini-turbo and spin turn as explicit driving techniques.
Items can disrupt rivals or boost the player and are described as tools that can turn the race; Deluxe allows two held items.
The product supports Grand Prix, Time Trial, VS Race and Battle, including local and online social play.
causalHypotheses: Core steering/drift skill gives repeatable mastery while items inject recoverability and tactical volatility.
Short races and fast restarts make social comparison and rematch cheap.
Readable track landmarks and strong movement feedback help a broad skill range understand immediate cause/effect.
transferHypotheses: Driving feel and item/catch-up dynamics should be tested separately before recombination.
references.smallestFalsifiableBaseline: One short three-lap track with drift/mini-boost and ghosts; then a matched condition adds position-sensitive disruptive/boost items.
references.baselineFalsifier: If the item condition does not change comeback possibility, route/risk decisions or social rematch behavior beyond adding noise, the catch-up hypothesis is weak.

references.title: Animal Crossing: New Horizons
observedFacts: Nintendo describes a self-paced island life built from gardening, fishing, decoration, collecting and relationships with animal residents.
Time of day and seasons track real life, so available activities and discoveries change over time.
The island develops from sparse beginnings as the player creates, collects and grows the community.
causalHypotheses: Real-time change creates a low-pressure return promise rather than demanding continuous sessions.
Persistent decoration and collection let routine actions accumulate into personal place attachment.
Weakly prescribed goals allow players to choose between collection, expression and social routines according to mood.
transferHypotheses: The return-promise and place-attachment claims can be tested with a tiny persistent room/island and real-time changes without large content volume.
references.smallestFalsifiableBaseline: One persistent small space with 3-4 daily activities, decoration, collection log, one resident acknowledgement and a real-time next-session change.
references.baselineFalsifier: If players do not form personal routines/place ownership or real-time change does not create return intention beyond checklist completion, the transfer is weak.

references.title: Candy Crush Saga
observedFacts: King describes Candy Crush Saga around switching and matching candies across a long sequence of levels.
Official community guidance describes adjacent swaps to make groups of three or more while satisfying level-specific goals within a limited move budget, with blockers and special candies.
causalHypotheses: A simple local action vocabulary becomes strategically varied when board goals, blockers and move scarcity change the value of the same swap.
Very short attempt cycles make failure/retry cheap and support mobile interruption patterns.
Progression can continually recontextualize a stable core rule without requiring a new control scheme.
transferHypotheses: The level-goal/move-budget grammar can be evaluated separately from monetization and live ops.
references.smallestFalsifiableBaseline: Ten original match-3 boards using one swap rule, two goal types, blockers, move limits and one special-piece combinator; no monetization or energy system.
references.baselineFalsifier: If changing goals/blockers does not materially change move evaluation or retry behavior, the stable-rule/recontextualization hypothesis is weak.

references.title: Beat Saber
observedFacts: Meta describes play as slashing, ducking and dodging in time with music while matching the color and direction of incoming notes.
Levels are handcrafted to music and use visual effects plus haptic feedback; the product is intrinsically embodied and hardware-dependent.
causalHypotheses: Binding beat prediction to directional whole-arm motion produces a tight perception-action loop that makes musical structure physically learnable.
Immediate audiovisual/haptic confirmation turns timing error into legible motor feedback.
Short songs naturally package attempts, mastery comparison and replay.
transferHypotheses: The core timing-direction claim cannot be validated by mouse/keyboard substitution; a lawful VR micro-beatmap is the minimum experiential carrier.
references.smallestFalsifiableBaseline: One 60-90 second original-audio VR beatmap with color/direction notes, dodge obstacles and immediate haptic/visual timing feedback.
references.baselineFalsifier: If directional embodied mapping does not improve timing anticipation, motor learning or replay desire versus a matched non-spatial rhythm control, the transfer is weak.

crossReferenceFindings: Successful products repeatedly combine a compact player-action grammar with a much larger context system; the context system differs by archetype.
Persistent success is often multiplexed: core interaction, content scale, social network, live ops, brand/IP and expression quality must remain separate causal candidates.
Several large products can be reduced to small causal experiments without treating the reduced experiment as a product clone.
Embodied feel, driving feel, combat timing, tension, agency and attachment remain experiential claims and are still unverified here.
